title: Wound cleaning and stitches
what: The doctor cleans the wound, removes dirt and damaged tissue, and stitches it if needed, under local anesthesia.
why: For cuts, torn wounds, puncture wounds, or bites, if the wound is deep, wide, keeps bleeding, or is dirty.
tell_doctor: When and how you got the wound
When you last had a tetanus shot
If an animal bit you: what animal, and where it is now
If you are allergic to numbing medicines or antibiotics

prepare.title: Stop the bleeding
prepare.text: Press the wound with a clean cloth or bandage and hold it for 10 to 15 minutes without letting go.

prepare.title: Do not
prepare.text: Do not pour powders into the wound, and do not put ointment or antiseptic dye inside it. Do not pull out an object stuck in the wound.

prepare.title: Do not delay
prepare.text: It is best to see a doctor within the first few hours. Then the wound can usually be stitched right away.

bring: Your vaccination records, if you have them
steps: The doctor checks the wound, and how you can move and feel
Numbing shots are given around the wound
The wound is rinsed and cleaned
If needed, damaged edges are trimmed
Stitches, skin tape strips, or medical glue are used to close it
A bandage is put on top
If needed, you get tetanus protection. After a bite, you are referred for a rabies vaccine
feel: The numbing shots sting for a few seconds, then the area goes numb
During stitching, you feel touch and pulling, but no sharp pain
When the numbing wears off, the wound will ache. Regular pain medicine helps
after: Change the bandage and get the wound wet only as your doctor said
Stitches are usually removed after 5 to 14 days: sooner on the face, later over joints
Come for wound checks and dressing changes on the set days
A small scar will remain. It fades over time
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop after 15 minutes of pressure: call emergency services
Spreading redness around the wound, pus, growing pain, or a fever are signs of infection
Numbness, or a finger below the wound will not move
A wound from an animal bite: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: After how many hours is it too late to stitch a wound?
faq.a: The sooner, the better. Usually within the first 6 to 12 hours, longer on the face. The doctor decides after checking it.
Usually after 5 to 14 days. Sooner on the face, later on the arms, legs, and over joints.
